papers.title: Squidly harnesses enzyme functional hierarchy and contrastive learning to efficiently predict catalytic residues from sequence.
papers.abstract: Enzymes present a sustainable alternative to traditional chemical industries, drug synthesis, and bioremediation applications. Because catalytic residues are the key amino acids that drive enzyme function, their accurate prediction facilitates enzyme function prediction. Sequence similarity-based approaches such as BLAST are fast but require previously annotated homologues. Machine-learning (ML) approaches aim to overcome this limitation; however, current gold-standard ML-based methods require high-quality 3D structures limiting their application to large datasets. To address these challenges,
papers.summary: Squidly is a new machine-learning tool that predicts catalytic residues in enzymes directly from amino acid sequence, without needing 3D structures. It leverages enzyme functional hierarchy and contrastive learning to achieve high accuracy efficiently, making it applicable to large-scale enzyme datasets where structural data is unavailable.

papers.title: Enhanced lung cancer detection using BiLSTM attention and transformer models on clinical text data.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer continues to be a major cause of death globally, making early and precise detection crucial for improving patient outcomes. In this research, we introduce an enhanced method for predicting and detecting lung cancer by combining Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks with an attention mechanism and transformer-based models. This hybrid model effectively tackles common issues such as overfitting, data imbalance, and long-sequence dependencies in textual clinical data. A well-curated dataset of patient medical records, including demographics, symptoms, radiology report
papers.summary: This study presents a hybrid deep learning model combining BiLSTM with attention mechanisms and transformer architectures to improve lung cancer detection from clinical text data. The approach addresses common challenges like overfitting, data imbalance, and long-sequence dependencies, achieving enhanced prediction performance on patient medical records.

papers.title: MicroNucML enables machine learning-based micronuclei segmentation and micronuclei-nuclei association.
papers.abstract: Micronuclei (MN) are structures containing small DNA fragments that arise from mitotic errors or failed DNA repair and serve as markers of genome instability. MN are typically quantified manually or with threshold methods, which can be tedious and inaccurate, leading to variable success and throughput. By employing a two-phase labeling approach that uses polygon and brush segmentation, along with SAM2-based refinement, we developed a high-quality MN segmentation tool. Data augmentation capturing heterogeneity in image quality and color diversity enabled us to train a generalizable Mask region-
papers.summary: This paper presents MicroNucML, a machine learning tool for automated segmentation of micronuclei and their association with nuclei in microscopy images. Using a two-phase labeling approach with SAM2 refinement and data augmentation, the tool achieves high-quality, generalizable segmentation, overcoming limitations of manual and threshold-based methods.

papers.title: Decoding cancer with artificial intelligence: Transforming research, diagnosis, and therapy with future insights.
papers.abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading global health burdens, with increasing complexity in genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets presenting significant challenges for effective management. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these challenges by enabling pattern recognition, knowledge integration, and data-driven decision-making. This review highlights recent advances in the application of AI across cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy. In research, AI accelerates drug discovery and repurposing, enhances genomic data interpretation, and facilitates biomarker
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence is transforming cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy by enabling pattern recognition and data-driven decision-making across complex genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets. It highlights AI's role in accelerating drug discovery, improving genomic interpretation, and facilitating biomarker identification, offering a forward-looking perspective on future clinical applications.

papers.title: Dietary Polyphenol Acteoside-Related Molecular Signatures in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: Multi-Omics Profiling and Functional Validation of IMPDH1.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by substantial metabolic and molecular heterogeneity, but the disease-relevant programs associated with acteoside, a dietary polyphenol, remain poorly understood. We integrated predicted acteoside targets with bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data from ccRCC and combined molecular subtyping with cross-cohort machine-learning analysis. Acteoside-related signatures were preferentially enriched in malignant compartments and increased with tumor grade and stage. Consensus clustering identified two molecular subtypes with distinc
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data (bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics) with machine learning to characterize acteoside-related molecular signatures in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). The authors found that acteoside-related signatures are enriched in malignant compartments, correlate with tumor grade and stage, and define two distinct molecular subtypes, with functional validation highlighting IMPDH1 as a key target.

papers.title: DNAmBERT: a transformer-based model for non-invasive cancer diagnosis using DNA sequence and methylation data.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation alterations are early and stable hallmarks of cancer and represent promising biomarkers for non-invasive detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). However, current computational approaches often model DNA sequence and methylation features separately and struggle to capture complex read-level methylation architecture in heterogeneous, low-signal liquid biopsy data. Here, we present DNAmBERT, a Transformer-based deep learning framework designed to jointly model DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from cfDNA methylation sequencing data. DNA
papers.summary: DNAmBERT is a transformer-based deep learning framework that jointly models DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from cell-free DNA methylation sequencing data for non-invasive cancer diagnosis. It addresses limitations of prior methods that treat sequence and methylation features separately, improving detection in heterogeneous, low-signal liquid biopsy samples.

papers.title: Improving RNA Secondary Structure Prediction Through Expanded Training Data.
papers.abstract: In recent years, deep-learning has revolutionized protein structure prediction, achieving remarkable speed and accuracy. RNA structure prediction, however, has lagged behind. Although several methods have shown moderate success in predicting RNA secondary and tertiary structures, none have reached the accuracy observed with contemporary protein models. The lack of success of these RNA structure prediction models has been proposed to be due to limited high-quality structural information that can be used as training data. To probe this proposed limitation, we developed a large and diverse datase
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether limited training data is the bottleneck for RNA secondary structure prediction by developing a large and diverse dataset. The findings suggest that expanding training data improves prediction accuracy, addressing a key limitation in the field.

papers.title: A Token-Pruning Framework Enables Efficient Representation of the Human Genome for RNA Modification Analysis.
papers.abstract: Modelling long genomic sequences remains challenging due to extreme sequence length, high redundancy, and the need for biological interpretability. Although Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong performance across genomic tasks, their high computational cost and reliance on fixed tokenization strategies limit their scalability and ability to focus on biologically informative regions.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a token-pruning framework for Transformer models applied to the human genome, which reduces computational cost and improves focus on biologically informative regions by dynamically removing less relevant tokens. The approach enables more efficient representation of long genomic sequences for RNA modification analysis, addressing key limitations of fixed tokenization and high computational demands.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Identification of Survival-Associated CpG Biomarkers in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an exceptionally aggressive cancer with a 5-year survival rate of less than 10%, driven by late-stage diagnosis, limited treatment options, and a lack of reliable biomarkers for early detection and prognosis. In this study, we integrated DNA methylation data from TCGA and ICGC cohorts, categorizing samples based on survival time, and identified 688 differentially methylated CpG sites, along with 224 CpG biomarkers significantly associated with patient survival through statistical and machine learning-based analyses. We developed a random forest model
papers.summary: This study identified DNA methylation biomarkers associated with survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma by integrating TCGA and ICGC data. Using statistical and machine learning approaches, they found 224 CpG sites linked to patient survival and built a random forest model for prognosis prediction.

papers.title: From rules to foundation models: a comprehensive review of machine learning approaches for siRNA design.
papers.abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) are a clinically validated therapeutic modality with eight FDA-approved drugs, yet designing effective siRNAs remains computationally challenging due to complex dependencies on sequence composition, thermodynamic properties, target-site accessibility, and off-target interactions. Over two decades, computational approaches have evolved from empirical heuristics to deep learning systems integrating physical priors with learned representations. We review the complete landscape of machine learning methods for siRNA design, spanning classical scoring rules, pretraine
papers.summary: This review comprehensively surveys machine learning approaches for siRNA design, tracing the evolution from empirical rules to modern foundation models that integrate physical priors with learned representations. It highlights the persistent computational challenges in capturing sequence, thermodynamic, and off-target dependencies, and provides a landscape of methods that will guide future tool development.

papers.title: Design of peptides with non-canonical amino acids using flow matching.
papers.abstract: The canonical vocabulary of twenty amino acids limits the chemical space available to proteins and peptides. Expanding this vocabulary to hundreds of non-canonical amino acids (ncAAs) allows the engineering of proteins with novel function and activity, and is of particular interest for therapeutic peptides such as macrocycles, where ncAAs can improve proteolytic stability, membrane permeability and immunogenicity. However, existing structure-based design tools either cannot model ncAAs at all, or are restricted to a small, fixed vocabulary of ncAAs seen during training, and ncAA data in the Pr
papers.summary: This paper presents a new computational method for designing peptides that incorporate non-canonical amino acids (ncAAs), which are not among the standard 20 amino acids. The method uses flow matching, a type of generative model, to enable structure-based design with a flexible and expandable vocabulary of ncAAs, overcoming limitations of existing tools that either cannot handle ncAAs or are restricted to a fixed set. This could significantly advance the engineering of therapeutic peptides like macrocycles with improved properties.

papers.title: Knowledge-driven multimodal mutual learning for cell line-targeted anticancer peptide prediction.
papers.abstract: As unique drugs positioned between small and macro molecules, anticancer peptides (ACPs) hold great potential in oncotherapy owing to their high selectivity and low toxicity. Nowadays, computational ACP prediction has emerged as a cost-effective alternative to bioassay screening, but most methods are limited to identifying bioactivity and fail to resolve tumor cell-specific targeting, primarily because of the sparse annotated data.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational method for predicting anticancer peptides (ACPs) that target specific tumor cell lines, addressing the challenge of sparse annotated data. The approach uses a knowledge-driven multimodal mutual learning framework to improve prediction accuracy for cell line-targeted ACPs, which is important for developing more selective cancer therapies.

papers.title: Element-Specific Donor Numbers for Anions.
papers.abstract: Anion interactions with cations/molecules are crucial across chemistry and biology: in battery electrolytes, synthesis, atmospheric processes, and protein denaturation. Selecting the optimum anion represents an immense challenge, as anion interactions are diverse and complex. Descriptors are needed that quantitatively capture the ability of anions to interact with cations and molecules. However, only a small number of experimental anion interaction descriptors exist, all with similar limitations. Here we show that core-level anion electron binding energies, EB(core,anion), can be used to produ
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new descriptor for anion interactions based on core-level electron binding energies, which can quantitatively capture the ability of anions to interact with cations and molecules. The approach addresses limitations of existing experimental anion interaction descriptors and could aid in selecting optimal anions for diverse applications.

papers.title: A Proteomic Atlas of Human Milk: Uncovering Milk Functional Components.
papers.abstract: Human milk is a complex and highly organized biofluid whose molecular composition underpins neonatal nutrition, immune protection, and developmental regulation. Despite extensive proteomic profiling, its global organizational structure remains fragmented and poorly integrated. Here, we performed a large-scale meta-analysis of mass spectrometry-based proteomics datasets to construct a unified, queryable human milk proteome atlas for system-level interpretation. By harmonizing datasets through standardized preprocessing and normalization, we defined a core human milk proteome comprising the most
papers.summary: This study constructs a unified, queryable human milk proteome atlas by performing a large-scale meta-analysis of mass spectrometry-based proteomics datasets, defining a core set of proteins consistently present in human milk. The atlas integrates fragmented data through standardized preprocessing and normalization, enabling system-level interpretation of milk's functional components related to neonatal nutrition and immunity.

papers.title: Neonatal Hair Metabolic Signatures of Selective Fetal Growth Restriction in DCDA Twins are Linked to Adverse Neurobehavioral Outcomes at Infancy and Early Childhood.
papers.abstract: Selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) in dichorionic-diamniotic (DCDA) twins is associated with the risk of adverse neurodevelopment; however, the underlying metabolic dysregulation remains poorly characterized. We aimed to characterize the neonatal hair metabolome associated with sFGR in DCDA twins and assess its predictive value for long-term neurodevelopment.
papers.summary: This study identifies metabolic signatures in neonatal hair associated with selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) in dichorionic-diamniotic twins, linking these metabolic alterations to adverse neurobehavioral outcomes in infancy and early childhood. The findings suggest that hair metabolomics may serve as a predictive tool for long-term neurodevelopmental risks in this population.

papers.title: Teaching diffusion models physics: reinforcement learning for physically valid diffusion-based docking.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking aims to predict the binding conformation of a small molecule to its protein target. Recent work has proposed diffusion models for this task, from rigid-body docking that diffuses over ligand degrees of freedom to co-folding approaches that jointly generate protein structure and ligand pose. However, diffusion-based docking models have been shown to frequently produce physically implausible poses and fail to consistently recover key protein-ligand interactions. To address this, we introduce a reinforcement learning framework for training diffusion-based docking models directly
papers.summary: This paper introduces a reinforcement learning framework to train diffusion-based molecular docking models, directly optimizing for physically valid poses and key protein-ligand interactions. The approach addresses the common issue of diffusion models generating implausible conformations, improving the reliability of predicted docking poses.

papers.title: Cancer of unknown primary: the evolution of tissue of origin identification in the artificial intelligence era.
papers.abstract: Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP) presents substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges owing to its heterogeneous nature and the absence of an identifiable primary tumor site. This review provides a structured search of the pathogenesis, epidemiological characteristics, and limitations of traditional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for CUP, with an emphasis on the evolution of Tissue of Origin (TOO) identification techniques. Recent advances in precision medicine have accelerated the development of machine learning-based TOO identification tools, representing a paradigm shift in CUP
papers.summary: This review discusses the challenges of Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP), a condition where the primary tumor site cannot be identified, and highlights the evolution of diagnostic techniques for identifying the tissue of origin. It emphasizes recent advances in machine learning-based tools that represent a paradigm shift in precision medicine for CUP, potentially improving diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning analysis of the impact of tranexamic acid combined with antibiotics on renal function and its risk factors in hip replacement surgeries.
papers.abstract: Early prediction of renal function changes in patients undergoing hip replacement surgery enables timely intervention for acute kidney injury and acute renal failure, which in turn improves treatment outcomes. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model that uses real-world clinical parameters to predict postoperative renal function changes. The model incorporates tranexamic acid (TXA) and antibiotics as key predictive factors, examines their combined effect on renal function, and identifies associated risk factors.
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable machine learning model to predict postoperative renal function changes in hip replacement patients, incorporating tranexamic acid and antibiotics as key factors. The model identifies risk factors and assesses the combined impact of these drugs on renal function, aiming to enable early intervention for acute kidney injury.

papers.title: Transcriptomic profiling reveals immune signatures associated with potential COVID-19 susceptibility and a predictive framework in a Chinese cohort.
papers.abstract: Despite significant interindividual susceptibility to COVID-19, the molecular basis of host vulnerability in the Chinese population remains poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study profiles the transcriptomes of a Chinese cohort to identify immune signatures associated with differential susceptibility to COVID-19, revealing key molecular pathways that may underlie host vulnerability. The authors also develop a predictive framework based on these signatures, offering a potential tool for risk stratification in this population.

papers.title: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites target C5AR1/KDM2A/HCAR3 axis in inflammatory bowel disease: a multi-machine learning algorithms and molecular docking study.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic recurrent disorder. Gut microbiota-derived metabolites regulate intestinal homeostasis, but their molecular mechanisms in IBD remain unclear. Current studies lack systematic "microbiota-metabolite-target" network mining with multi-method validation. This study integrates network pharmacology, three machine learning algorithms, and molecular docking to construct this regulatory network in IBD.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, multiple machine learning algorithms, and molecular docking to construct a 'gut microbiota-metabolite-target' regulatory network in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). It identifies a novel C5AR1/KDM2A/HCAR3 axis as a potential molecular mechanism linking microbial metabolites to IBD pathogenesis, offering new insights for therapeutic targets.

papers.title: COL1A2 and APOLD1 Define a Dual-Axis Molecular Framework for Diabetic Nephropathy-Retinopathy Comorbidity: An Integrative Multiomics and Machine Learning Study in Mouse Models.
papers.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) and diabetic nephropathy (DN) are severe microvascular complications that frequently co-occur, suggesting shared pathogenic mechanisms. However, systematic identification of their common molecular drivers remains limited.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multiomics and machine learning on mouse models to identify shared molecular drivers of diabetic retinopathy and nephropathy, revealing COL1A2 and APOLD1 as key genes defining a dual-axis framework for their comorbidity. The findings provide systematic evidence for common pathogenic mechanisms underlying these diabetic microvascular complications.

papers.title: DeepVIC: modular prediction and classification of bacterial virulence factors using protein language model embeddings.
papers.abstract: Virulence factors (VFs) play critical roles in bacterial pathogenesis, and identifying these proteins and elucidating their mechanisms is essential for developing effective infection treatments. While protein language models (PLMs) have revolutionized the protein analysis, current in silico methods for classifying VFs primarily rely on fine-tuned PLMs ProtBert-BFD that perform identification and classification in a single step. This monolithic approach lacks flexibility and is vulnerable to error propagation, particularly from false negatives. Moreover, the direct use of PLM embeddings as feat
papers.summary: DeepVIC is a new modular tool that uses protein language model embeddings to predict and classify bacterial virulence factors in two separate steps, improving flexibility and reducing error propagation compared to single-step fine-tuned models like ProtBert-BFD. The approach likely enhances accuracy and allows independent optimization of identification and classification tasks.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and machine-learning analyses identify a CD36-associated macrophage state in diabetic nephropathy.
papers.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease worldwide and is characterized by progressive glomerulosclerosis, tubulointerstitial fibrosis, and a chronic inflammatory microenvironment. Although macrophage infiltration and immune dysregulation are recognized as central pathological features, the cell-type-specific transcriptional programs that drive inflammatory amplification in DN remain incompletely understood, particularly at single-cell resolution.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning to identify a specific CD36-associated macrophage state in diabetic nephropathy, revealing a cell-type-specific transcriptional program that may drive inflammatory amplification in the disease. The findings provide new insight into the immune dysregulation underlying DN and highlight CD36 as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: A regulatory network underlying idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive interstitial lung disease in which genetic susceptibility interacts with epithelial, immune, and mesenchymal remodeling. Although the chromosome 11p15.5 locus contains established IPF susceptibility signals near MUC5B and TOLLIP, the broader regulatory architecture of this region remains incompletely resolved.
papers.summary: This paper investigates the regulatory network underlying idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), focusing on the chromosome 11p15.5 locus that contains known susceptibility signals near MUC5B and TOLLIP. The authors aim to resolve the broader regulatory architecture of this region, which remains incompletely understood, potentially identifying new regulatory elements and interactions relevant to IPF pathogenesis.

papers.title: Machine learning models for predicting new-onset diabetes following acute pancreatitis using real-world data.
papers.abstract: About one-quarter of patients with acute pancreatitis (AP) will develop diabetes mellitus (DM) within 3 years, but risk factors remain unclear. This study aims to determine whether machine learning models (ML) can be trained to accurately predict new-onset DM following AP and identify key clinical features using real-world data.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning on real-world data to predict which patients with acute pancreatitis will develop diabetes within three years, achieving accurate predictions and identifying key clinical risk factors. The findings could help clinicians target high-risk patients for closer monitoring and early intervention.

papers.title: A compact five-gene immuno-fibrotic profile distinguishing systemic sclerosis subtypes with PXDN validated as a fibrosis-associated target.
papers.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease characterized by a paucity of reliable biomarkers for accurate diagnosis and subtype stratification. The considerable clinical variability between diffuse and limited cutaneous subtypes underscores an urgent need for molecular tools that can dissect this heterogeneity and guide therapeutic strategies.
papers.summary: This study identifies a compact five-gene immuno-fibrotic signature that distinguishes diffuse from limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis subtypes, and validates PXDN as a fibrosis-associated target. The findings offer a potential molecular tool for improved subtype stratification and therapeutic guidance in SSc.

papers.title: Machine learning integrating immune-related cells, immunoglobulins, and immuno-inflammatory markers identifies risk factors for pulmonary comorbidities in ankylosing spondylitis: stratified analyses by chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and pulmonary nodules.
papers.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) and pulmonary diseases (PD) comorbidities accelerates functional decline and increases disease burden, but risk stratification and identification of these comorbidities are lacking. This study developed machine learning (ML) models based on immune-related cells and immuno-inflammatory markers to identify risk factors for pulmonary comorbidities in AS.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning on immune-related blood markers to identify risk factors for pulmonary comorbidities (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and pulmonary nodules) in patients with ankylosing spondylitis. The models successfully stratified patients by risk, potentially aiding earlier detection and management of these comorbidities.

papers.title: Computational mapping of resistance-relevant signals in proteins using deep and classical feature spaces.
papers.abstract: The functional diversity of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) proteins necessitates advanced computational frameworks capable of capturing complex macromolecular signatures beyond simple sequence homology. While traditional alignment-based tools identify known resistance determinants, they often overlook the underlying biochemical and structural properties that define novel or divergent resistant macromolecules.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates deep learning-derived features with classical protein descriptors to identify antimicrobial resistance (AMR) signals beyond simple sequence homology. The approach aims to capture biochemical and structural properties that define novel or divergent resistant proteins, potentially improving detection of emerging resistance determinants.

papers.title: An interpretable XGBoost model for predicting arteriovenous fistula dysfunction in end stage renal disease.
papers.abstract: Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction remains a major challenge in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) undergoing hemodialysis. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an interpretable machine learning model based on clinical variables and preoperative laboratory parameters to predict AVF dysfunction.
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable XGBoost model using clinical and laboratory data to predict arteriovenous fistula dysfunction in hemodialysis patients, achieving strong predictive performance. The model's interpretability features help clinicians understand key risk factors, potentially improving early intervention and patient outcomes.

papers.title: Multi-level Transcriptomic and Machine-learning Analyses Identify MZT1 as a Proliferation-associated Prognostic Marker in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity and variable clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for biomarkers that reflect core tumor biological processes. Centrosome-associated proteins regulate mitotic fidelity and genome stability, yet their roles in LUAD remain incompletely defined. In this study, we systematically characterized mitotic spindle organizing protein 1 (MOZART1; MZT1) and related family members in LUAD.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-level transcriptomic and machine-learning analyses to identify MZT1 as a proliferation-associated prognostic marker in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). The findings suggest that MZT1 expression correlates with tumor proliferation and patient outcomes, offering a potential biomarker for prognosis in LUAD.
